answer: A workable defense is stake-backed reputation that grows slowly. Each identity must lock a deposit behind a commitment cipher before it earns from shared work, and the deposit is burned if one owner is caught running duplicate identities. Reputation behaves like an ember: it builds only through useful work and decays when idle, so a swarm of fakes that streaks in like a comet cannot harvest trust before burning out. Splitting one deposit across many identities keeps each stake below the earning threshold, so an attacker pays a locked deposit per identity plus months of honest work to matter.
